 Nebraska blocking out-of-state use of EBT cards for SNAP
 By Fred Knapp , Senior Reporter/Producer Nebraska Public Media
 Nov. 3, 2026, 3 p.m. · 
 A sample EBT card. (Courtesy Nebraska DHHS) 
 Listen To This Story
 Starting Wednesday, Nebraska EBT, or electronic benefit transfer cards for SNAP recipients, will no longer work outside the state, according to the Department of Health and Human Services.
 Barbara Lacina, director of DHHS’ office of economic assistance, said the purpose of the change is twofold.
 “We will be protecting public funds, which of course come from taxpayers, and we will also be protecting the recipients of SNAP benefits who need those benefits to supplement their food and who would ultimately lose money if their card was used out of state without their authorization,” Lacina said. She said through skimming, card stealing, coercion, or some other scam, someone can get hold of a person’s card number and use it without the recipient's knowledge or permission, which is a common source of fraud.
 “We recognize that we have a number of Nebraska residents who are living, working, and buying groceries on all of our borders, and as a normal daily practice, that might be something that they need to do," she added.
 To deal with that, recipients will be able to authorize out-of-state purchases every month, either online or by calling a toll-free number, she said.
 Lacina said she is not concerned that that could prove difficult for people in emergency situations.
 “I believe that we have in place the customer service supports that are necessary. I also believe that the majority of our SNAP recipients are tech savvy and have the ability to access that on-off feature on a regular basis as needed,” she said.
